assertions.name: health-endpoint-200
openapi-contract-200
assertions.outputSample:
HTTP 200
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Lost & Found Service API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: >
    Endpoints exposed by Team 10 (Lost & Found) for consumption by Team 11
    (Inventory) to look up, search, and reconcile found items against
    missing inventory records.

servers:
  - url: /
    description: This server (works on Render and on localhost)
  - url: https://api-programming.onrender.com
    description: Public deployment (Render)
  - url: http://localhost:5000
    description: Local development

paths:
  /health:
    get:
      security:
        - ApiKeyAuth: []
      summary: Check API and database availability.
      description: Requires a valid API key.
      responses:
        '200':
          description: API and database are available.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [status, database]
                properties:
                  status:
                    type: string
                    example: ok
                  database:
                    type: string
                    example: connected
        '503':
          description: API is running but the database is unavailable.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [status, database]
                properties:
                  status:
                    type: string
                    example: error
                  database:
                    type: string
                    example: unavailable
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        '403':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/RateLimited'

  /found-items/{itemId}:
    get:
      security:
        - ApiKeyAuth: []
      summary: Retrieve a single found-item record by its ID.
      description: Requires the `items:read` API-key scope.
      parameters:
        - name: itemId
          in: path
          required: true
          description: Unique identifier of the found item.
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
            example: "7c3f2a10-9e21-4b3d-8a4a-2f6b1c9d0e11"
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Found item located successfully.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/FoundItem'
              example:
                itemId: "7c3f2a10-9e21-4b3d-8a4a-2f6b1c9d0e11"
                status: "unclaimed"
                location: "Library, 2nd Floor Front Desk"
                dateFound: "2026-08-13T10:00:00Z"
                description: "Black umbrella with wooden handle"
                category: "personal-items"
        '404':
          description: No found item exists with the given ID (an ID that is not a valid UUID is treated as not found).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
              example:
                error: "not_found"
                message: "No found item exists with ID 7c3f2a10-9e21-4b3d-8a4a-2f6b1c9d0e11."
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        '403':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/RateLimited'

  /found-items:
    get:
      security:
        - ApiKeyAuth: []
      summary: >
        Browse, search, or sync the found-items table. Read-only —
        no create, update, or delete operations are exposed on this path.
      description: Requires the `items:read` API-key scope.
      parameters:
        - name: category
          in: query
          required: false
          description: Filter found items by category. Used with `keyword` when an exact ID match is uncertain.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [electronics, personal-items, documents, clothing, keys, other]
            example: "electronics"
        - name: keyword
